parameters.content:
Market session plan for Monday, Oct 12:
- Goal: cover $20 entry fee, protect cash balance, and sell through higher-margin items while keeping inventory variety.
- Inventory strategy: no new supplier orders before the session (cash conservation). Focus on selling current stock: chopsticks, dried noodles, miso paste, rice, sesame oil, soap, soy sauce.
- Pricing & negotiation: start at listed prices. Allow haggling—accept offers down to roughly cost + 15% for low-margin items and cost + 30% for higher-margin items, depending on customer. Be flexible to close sales.
- Promotions/bundles: offer small bundles to increase basket size (suggested: ramen + miso bundle at a small discount; rice + soy sauce pairing; buy 2 soaps get small discount). Consider including a free soap for purchases over a set threshold to encourage larger buys.
- Sales focus: prioritize miso, sesame oil, and rice for margin; use noodles and soy sauce as easy add-ons.
- Service: friendly greetings, quick demos of product uses, and willingness to haggle. Track who buys what to tailor future offers.
- Post-session: review ledger and inventory; if cash allows later in the week, consider restocking top sellers through Hayashi Supply.

parameters.content:
Strategy for Monday, Oct 12 — Corner Provisions

Goals
- Ensure we can pay the $20 entry fee and make incremental profit. Target at least $40 in sales (covers fee + small profit).
- Preserve a $20 cash buffer for entry fee; avoid supplier spending that would drop below $20 before next open.

Pricing and negotiation
- Listed prices set (ceramic_bowl $12, dried_seaweed $8, green_tea $12, incense $7, matcha $18, pickled_ginger $5, rice $10).
- Haggling rules (informal): accept offers down to these suggested floors when needed to close a sale: ceramic_bowl $9, dried_seaweed $6, green_tea $9, incense $5, matcha $14, pickled_ginger $4, rice $8. Be willing to bundle for small discounts.
- Bundles/promos to push volume: “Rice + Pickled Ginger” for $13 (saves $2); “Tea + Incense” for $17 (saves $2). Offer a free pickled_ginger as small promo only when it secures a larger purchase (use exact item name pickled_ginger if added to a formal deal).

Inventory and restock plan
- No urgent restock required for Monday; current stock should cover likely traffic.
- If customers ask for items we don’t have (soy_sauce, miso_paste, sesame_oil, chopsticks, candles, etc.), note requests and consider ordering after close from Hayashi Supply. Supplier orders arrive after two calendar days; plan for availability at the next open session if ordered after Monday.
- Maintain conservative ordering: don’t commit more than $40 to supplier orders before verifying Monday sales.

Operations
- Bring clear price tags and bundle signs. Keep change ready and small freebies (one pickled_ginger jars) reserved for promotions only.
- Track customer preferences and one-off requests for post-market supplier orders.

If sales are slow
- Emphasize bundles and small discounts to convert browsers.
- Reduce listed-floor margins by $1–2 if needed to move product, starting with incense and pickled_ginger.

End of plan.

parameters.content:
Goal: Cover the $20 entry fee and make modest profit; keep prices attractive for haggling. Sales targets: move 8–12 units across categories.

Pricing & Haggling strategy
- Listed prices (already set): chopsticks $7, dried_seaweed $8, green_tea $12, incense $8, miso_paste $9, rice $10, soap $6.
- Negotiation floors (minimum acceptable): chopsticks $5, dried_seaweed $6, green_tea $9, incense $6, miso_paste $6, rice $8, soap $4. Be flexible for bundle deals.

Promotions
- Offer a free Handmade Yuzu Soap (soap) with any single purchase over $18 (use stock soap). Try to use this to close higher-value sales while clearing small inventory.
- Bundle suggestion: 2 rice for $18 if customers ask for a bulk discount.

Inventory & Restock
- Current stock is sufficient for opening; do not place supplier orders before seeing demand. If an item sells out (especially rice, green_tea, or miso_paste), plan to reorder from Hayashi Supply after market close.

Customer service
- Greet customers warmly, encourage haggling, and be willing to split margins to close deals—prioritize selling higher-margin items (green_tea, miso_paste, rice).
- Watch competitor stalls and adjust on the fly if needed.

Post-market
- Review sales and place standard catalog orders (order_from_supplier) for items that sold well. For any specialty requests, message Hayashi Supply privately and negotiate a place_supplier_order if needed.

Note: Keep at least $20 available to pay the entry fee for the next market session.

- Opening notes: Entry fee $20 will be paid from $80 cash. Keep enough float (~$20) for change and small concessions.

- Sales priorities: Move Dried Ramen Noodles, Soy Sauce, Beeswax Candles first (high turnover + good margins). Promote giftable household items (furoshiki, tenugui) to late-morning shoppers.

- Pricing & haggling strategy: Start at listed prices. Be willing to accept these minimums during negotiation to keep volume:
  • Beeswax Candles (list $10): accept down to $7
  • Dried Ramen Noodles (list $7): accept down to $5
  • Furoshiki (list $9): accept down to $6
  • Sesame Oil (list $8): accept down to $6
  • Soy Sauce (list $5): accept down to $4
  • Tenugui (list $7): accept down to $5
  • Umeboshi (list $9): accept down to $7

- Promotions to offer in-person:
  • Ramen Kit: Dried Noodles + Soy Sauce for $10 (regular $12) — positioned as quick lunch kit.
  • Buy 2 household items (furoshiki/tenugui) get $2 off total.
  • Small volume discount: 10% off purchases over $20.

- Operations notes: Have clear signage for bundle deals. Keep small change and a calculator app ready. Watch competitor stalls for overlapping prices and adjust next session if undercut.

After the market, review sales and consider ordering more dried_noodles and soy_sauce from Hayashi Supply if they sell well. Tuesday, Oct 13 strategy — Corner Provisions

Goals
- Ensure we can pay $20 entry fee and keep $20 buffer. Target at least $40 in sales.
- Continue incremental profit and preserve inventory for high-margin items.

Pricing & Promotions
- Keep listed prices same as Monday: ceramic_bowl $12, dried_seaweed $8, green_tea $12, incense $7, matcha $18, pickled_ginger $5, rice $10.
- Floors unchanged: ceramic_bowl $9, dried_seaweed $6, green_tea $9, incense $5, matcha $14, pickled_ginger $4, rice $8.
- Bundles: Rice + Pickled Ginger $13; Tea + Incense $17. Free pickled_ginger with purchases over $25 (one jar) to drive larger sales.

Inventory & Restock priorities (based on customer requests today)
- High interest items: chashu pork (Haruki), ceremony-quality bamboo whisk (Tomoko), soy_sauce (Kenji/Mei), miso_paste (Haruki/Ryo), umeboshi (Kenji), toasted_sesame_oil.
- Conservative supplier ordering plan: request Hayashi quotes after market close for these items; do NOT commit more than $40 total before quotes and approvals.
- Initial quote requests (suggested quantities): chashu pork x2, ceremony-quality bamboo whisk x1 (ask for ceremony grade first), soy_sauce (500ml) x4, miso_paste (500g) x4, umeboshi plums (jar) x2, toasted_sesame_oil (250ml) x2. Decide after quotes which to buy, prioritise soy/miso/whisk/chashu in that order.

Operations
- Keep change ready, signage for bundles, and reserve one pickled_ginger jar for promotions.
- Note customers who asked for items: Haruki (chashu, miso, sesame oil, noodles), Kenji (soy, umeboshi), Tomoko (whisk, tea), Mei (rice/noodles/soy). Use this to prioritise supplier quotes and outreach.

Supplier negotiation policy
- Write privately to Hayashi Supply to request item availability, unit cost, shipping/fees, and ETA (2 calendar days standard). Ask explicitly whether the bamboo whisk can be ceremony-quality and provide price cap for automatic purchase (e.g., Tomoko’s cap $24).
- Only place supplier orders (place_supplier_order) after receiving and approving quotes; total committed spend across all orders must not exceed $40 before verifying Monday sales.

Next steps (preparation time)
1) After writing this plan, message Hayashi Supply privately during preparation to request quotes for prioritized items (chashu, ceremony whisk, soy, miso, umeboshi, sesame oil) — include requested quantities and ask total cost + ETA.
2) Review quotes and decide which orders to place without dropping cash below $20.
3) Set prices (no change) and prepare stall for Tuesday.

If sales are slow on Tuesday: emphasize bundles and be willing to move incense and pickled_ginger floors by $1–2 to convert browsers.

Market plan for Tuesday, Oct 13, 2026

1) Goals
- Cover $20 entry fee and protect cash balance ($83 cash on hand).
- Push higher-margin items: Miso Paste, Toasted Sesame Oil, Short-grain Rice.
- Increase basket size with small, compelling bundles and a free-soap promotion for larger purchases.
- Avoid new supplier orders during preparation to conserve cash; re-evaluate mid-week if cash > $100.

2) Inventory snapshot (end of Mon 10/12):
- Lacquered Chopstick Set: 5 units (cost $3 each)
- Dried Ramen Noodles (6-pack): 8 units (cost $3 each)
- Miso Paste (500g): 8 units (cost $3 each)
- Short-grain Rice (2kg bag): 9 units (cost $4 each)
- Toasted Sesame Oil (250ml): 6 units (cost $3 each)
- Handmade Yuzu Soap (bar): 6 units (cost $2 each)
- Soy Sauce (500ml): 9 units (cost $2 each)
Cash: $83.00 (next market entry fee $20)

3) Pricing (listed; keep same for tomorrow)
- Lacquered Chopstick Set: $6.00
- Dried Ramen Noodles (6-pack): $7.00
- Miso Paste (500g): $8.00
- Short-grain Rice (2kg bag): $10.00
- Toasted Sesame Oil (250ml): $8.00
- Handmade Yuzu Soap (bar): $4.00
- Soy Sauce (500ml): $5.00

4) Bundles & Promotions (to offer on-stall)
- Rice + Soy Sauce for $14 (small savings vs $15).
- Miso + Noodles for $13 (vs $15).
- Miso + Sesame Oil for $14 (vs $16).
- Buy 2 Soaps for $7 (vs $8).
- Free Handmade Yuzu Soap (bar) for purchases over $25 to encourage larger baskets (while stock lasts).

5) Negotiation policy (guidelines for haggling)
- Start at listed prices; be willing to accept modest discounts.
- Low-margin items (soap, soy sauce, chopsticks, noodles): accept down to roughly cost + 15% if needed to close a sale.
- Higher-margin items (miso, sesame oil, rice): accept down to roughly cost + 30% for price-sensitive customers.
- Use bundles and free soap promo to preserve margins while giving customers perceived value.

6) Sales focus & tactics
- Greet customers, highlight miso, sesame oil, and rice first.
- Offer quick-use suggestions (miso ramen, dressings with sesame oil, rice pairings).
- Offer bundles proactively when customers buy one of the pair items.
- Hold items on request for short periods; be willing to set aside best-sellers to close sales.
- Track who buys what to tailor next visits and future offers.

7) Supplier & restock policy
- Hayashi Supply is primary supplier (2 calendar day lead time).
- No standard catalog supplier orders tonight to conserve cash.
- If cash exceeds $100 mid-week, consider ordering additional Miso Paste or Rice from Hayashi.
- For specialty requests (chashu, umeboshi, matcha) accept customer orders and place supplier orders after market close only if the customer confirms and is willing to cover supplier cost + fee.

8) Cash management
- Maintain at least $20 cash to pay tomorrow's entry fee.
- Preserve cash; avoid restocking unless clear demand and cash buffer > $100.

Notes: Ready to set prices tomorrow at the listed levels and focus on margin items. Re-evaluate mid-week depending on sales and cash flow.

Tuesday, Oct 13 strategy — Corner Provisions

Goals
- Ensure we can pay the $20 entry fee and keep a $20 cash buffer. Target at least $40 in sales for the day.
- Continue incremental profit while preserving stock of higher-margin items.

Cash & Inventory Snapshot (after Oct 12)
- Cash on hand: $152.00. Keep $20 reserved for entry fee; avoid spending that would drop below $20.
- Inventory (approx.): Ceramic Rice Bowl (ceramic_bowl): 4 units, Dried Seaweed Sheets (dried_seaweed): 10 units, Loose Leaf Green Tea (green_tea): 7 units, Sandalwood Incense (incense): 7 units, Matcha Powder (matcha): 2 units, Pickled Ginger (pickled_ginger): 5 units, Short-grain Rice (rice): 7 units.

Pricing & Promotions (no changes)
- Listed prices: ceramic_bowl $12, dried_seaweed $8, green_tea $12, incense $7, matcha $18, pickled_ginger $5, rice (2kg) $10.
- Negotiation floors: ceramic_bowl $9, dried_seaweed $6, green_tea $9, incense $5, matcha $14, pickled_ginger $4, rice $8.
- Bundles/promos: Rice + Pickled Ginger jar $13; Tea + Incense $17. Free pickled_ginger jar with purchases over $25 (limit one per qualifying purchase).
- If traffic is slow, be willing to reduce incense and pickled_ginger floors by $1–2 to convert browsers.

Restock priorities (based on customer requests today)
- Highest customer interest: chashu_pork (Haruki), ceremony-quality bamboo whisk (Tomoko), soy_sauce (Kenji/Mei), miso_paste (Haruki/Ryo), umeboshi_plums (Kenji), toasted_sesame_oil (Haruki).
- Conservative supplier spending cap: do not commit more than $40 total before getting quotes and confirming the next-day cash buffer.

Initial supplier quote requests (to ask Hayashi Supply during preparation)
- Chashu Pork x2 (ask for price per unit, total cost, and ETA).
- Bamboo Whisk (chasen) ceremony-quality x1 (explicitly ask for ceremony-grade; if not available, best-quality alternative). Note Tomoko’s automatic approval cap: $24 total incl. shipping/fees.
- Soy Sauce (500ml) x4.
- Miso Paste (500g) x4.
- Umeboshi Plums (jar) x2.
- Toasted Sesame Oil (250ml) x2.
- Ask Hayashi for unit cost, shipping/fees, and ETA (standard lead time two calendar days). Tell Hayashi we will confirm before placing orders; do not place orders automatically except where pre-authorised.

Supplier ordering policy
- During preparation, privately request quotes from Hayashi Supply for the prioritized list. Do not place any orders until quotes are received and reviewed.
- Commit to placing supplier orders only if total committed spend will not drop cash below $20 and total pre-confirm spend ≤ $40.
- For Tomoko’s ceremony whisk: only place automatically if Hayashi confirms ceremony-quality and total cost ≤ $24; otherwise send the quote to Tomoko for approval.

Operations & Sales Plan for Tuesday
- Keep prices and bundle signage visible. Reserve one pickled_ginger jar for promotions.
- Emphasize bundles to increase average sale value (Rice+Pickled Ginger, Tea+Incense). Offer free pickled_ginger on purchases > $25 to incentivize bundles (one per sale).
- Prioritise selling lower-margin/fast-moving items (incense, pickled_ginger) if traffic is slow; be willing to reduce floors by $1–2 starting with incense and pickled_ginger.
- Track customer requests and note any repeated demand to inform next supplier round.

Next steps (preparation time now)
1) Send private quote request to Hayashi Supply for the prioritized items and quantities (do not place orders yet). Include Tomoko’s whisk quality requirement and automatic approval cap.
2) Set prices unchanged for Tuesday and prepare stall signage.
3) When quotes arrive, decide which orders to place without dropping cash below $20 and keeping total spend ≤ $40.
4) Open for Tuesday with the above pricing, bundles, and promotional policy.

Contingencies
- If quotes push projected cash below $20, postpone orders and prioritise soy/miso/whisk in next round.
- If sales are slow during Tuesday, increase promotional emphasis and accept lower offers within floor limits to hit minimum sales target.

Notes
- Keep good records of customer requests (Haruki, Kenji, Tomoko, Mei) to prioritise future restocks.
- After writing this plan, the next action will be to message Hayashi Supply privately to request quotes (during preparation).

parameters.content:
Canopy Goods — Preparation plan for Tuesday, Oct 13 (market opens 9:00)

1) Cash & entry fee
- Cash on hand: $108.00. Tomorrow's entry fee: $20.00 — set aside on arrival. Maintain float ~$20 for change and concessions. Target usable cash for restock: $108 - $20 (entry) - $20 (float) = $68.

2) End-of-day inventory (after Monday sales)
- Beeswax Candles (set of 4): 8 units
- Dried Ramen Noodles (6-pack): 8 units
- Furoshiki Wrapping Cloth: 4 units
- Toasted Sesame Oil (250ml): 3 units
- Soy Sauce (500ml): 6 units
- Tenugui Hand Towel: 6 units
- Umeboshi Plums (jar): 5 units

3) Pricing & haggling thresholds (keep same; start at listed prices)
- Beeswax Candles: list $10, floor $7
- Dried Ramen Noodles: list $7, floor $5
- Furoshiki: list $9, floor $6
- Sesame Oil: list $8, floor $6
- Soy Sauce: list $5, floor $4
- Tenugui: list $7, floor $5
- Umeboshi: list $9, floor $7

Promotions to run in-person
- Ramen Kit: Dried Noodles + Soy Sauce $10 (regular $12)
- Buy 2 household items (furoshiki/tenugui) get $2 off total
- 10% off purchases over $20

4) Sales priorities & tactics
- Priority items to push: Dried Ramen Noodles, Soy Sauce, Beeswax Candles (high turnover + margins).
- Lead with the Ramen Kit at midday lunch. Use 10–15 minute holds to close tentative customers.
- Accept bundle offers down to agreed floors to keep volume, especially for noodle/soy combos.

5) Restock recommendations (based on today’s demand and cash position)
- Primary restock targets: Dried Ramen Noodles and Soy Sauce. Recommend ordering +5–10 units each depending on supplier price and minimums. 
- Secondary: Sesame Oil (low stock: 3 units) — consider reorder if supplier minimums/prices are reasonable.
- Preserve enough cash to pay entry fee and maintain float; do not spend more than ~$50–60 before the next open session unless margin is clearly profitable.

6) Supplier & special orders
- Hayashi quote requested for Yuki: 1 small student/travel Watercolor Set + options (tiny brush, metal mixing tin, small sample color set). Wait for Hayashi reply and Yuki confirmation; if total ≤ $21 and Yuki confirms, place order after market close so it arrives in two calendar days.
- Haruki/others may request Chashu Pork, Miso, or Dried Seaweed — lead time two calendar days. Offer quotes if requested and place orders after the market if customer approves.
- When placing restock orders, confirm Hayashi minimum order qty, unit price, and shipping/fees before committing.

7) Operational notes
- Signage: highlight Ramen Kit and the Buy 2 household items discount. Post small signs showing bargaining floors discreetly (helps anchor offers).
- Hold policy: reserve items for 10–15 minutes on request; mark held items to avoid double-selling.
- Keep calculator and change float ~ $20. Track competitor prices and adjust next session if undercut.

8) Post-market actions (tomorrow morning preparation)
- Review updated ledger and inventory, set prices (no change expected), place any approved Hayashi orders based on quotes and customer confirmations, and ensure $20 set aside for entry fee.
- If supplier quotes for restock look good, prefer ordering +5 dried_noodles and +5 soy_sauce (adjust to minimums/prices). Avoid over-ordering until we confirm demand.

Prepared by: Canopy Goods — ready to place approved supplier orders after quotes and customer confirmation.

- Opening sign: list core items and bundles, advertise free pickled_ginger > $25 (one per sale). Emphasize bundles to lift average sale value.

- Early day: promote Tea+Incense and Rice+Pickled Ginger combos. Midday/lull: use short, visible limited-time discounts on incense/pickled_ginger if traffic slow (e.g., -$1 for one-hour windows). Late-day: repeat final-hours push to hit daily sales target of ≥ $40.
- Haggling: accept reasonable offers at/above negotiation floors; prefer to preserve high-margin matcha and bowls unless customer willing to meet closer to list.

6) Restock decision logic when quotes arrive
- Review itemized totals from Hayashi (unit price + shipping/fees + any deposit). Compare combined spend to conservative cap $40 and ensure cash remains ≥ $20 after commit.
- If multiple items fit, prioritise Soy Sauce and Miso Paste first, then Chasen (only with Tomoko approval), then Umeboshi/Toasted Sesame Oil, then Chashu if refrigerated shipping cost acceptable and total within cap.
- If Hayashi lists a ceremony chasen priced ≤ $24 total and Tomoko consents to auto-approve earlier (she opted for quote-first), we will still forward it to her per her request; do not auto-place.

- Morning prep (before market opens): set_prices (leave as above), prepare signage, confirm reserve pickled_ginger jar.

- Keep ledger updated for any supplier spend. Maintain $20 minimum cash buffer at all times.

8) Contingencies
- If quotes would drop cash below $20: postpone orders and prioritise soy/miso/chasen next round.
- If sales remain slow: extend limited-time discounts, accept near-floor offers on incense/pickled_ginger to reach daily $40 target.

- I’m ready to open Wed with current pricing and promos, awaiting Hayashi’s quotes to decide restocking. After reviewing any quotes and placing any approved orders, call wait_for_next_day to advance to the next market session.

- Cover $20 entry fee and preserve a cash buffer (current cash $108).

- Free Handmade Yuzu Soap (bar) for purchases over $25 while stock lasts

- Greet customers, lead with miso, sesame oil, and rice.

- Offer free soap over $25 to increase basket size.
- Track customer preferences for follow-up and supplier quote requests.

Market General — Plan for next market session (Wednesday):

1) Financials & risk management
- Cash on hand: $67. Reserve $20 immediately for market entry fee, leaving $47 available for supplier orders or opportunistic buys. Avoid any supplier commitments that would reduce cash below the $20 reserve.

2) Supplier actions (pending Hayashi replies)
- Chashu (one pack for Haruki): place order only if Hayashi’s firm total to me ≤ $29 (Haruki already confirmed). If quoted ≤ $29, place the order after I receive the firm quote and charge Haruki or record sale accordingly.
- Eggs small pack & Tofu 300g (for Mei): place supplier orders only if Hayashi’s firm totals to me are ≤ $5 and ≤ $4 respectively (Mei’s caps). If either meets the cap, place order and notify Mei of ETA (2‑day lead typical).
- Ask Hayashi whether combining items (chashu/eggs/tofu) reduces fees; if combined pricing reduces total and still meets customer caps, place combined order only if it respects the $20 reserve.

3) Pricing & promotions for next session
- Keep most prices the same. Small adjustments to stay competitive: lower listed Miso Paste (500g) from $9 → $8 to match Lantern Pantry’s $8 and make us competitive (cost $3, still healthy margin). Lower Sandalwood Incense (30) from $8 → $7 to remain close to Corner Provisions’ quick deal.
- Offer a temporary bundle: Miso Paste + Dried Seaweed for $14 (listed $8+$8=$16) to encourage bundles and compete with neighbor bundles.
- Promo: First two customers who buy over $15 get a Handmade Yuzu Soap free (use stocked soap as promotion; include exact item name when completing sale).

4) Inventory & restock priorities
- Keep a minimum on-hand: Miso ≥5, Dried Seaweed ≥5, Loose Leaf Green Tea ≥4. Current stock is adequate; revisit restock if Hayashi quotes for bulk miso/seaweed are attractive and don’t endanger reserve.
- No urgent restock required for tea (5 units) or rice (8 units).

5) Customer service & negotiation plan
- Hold items requested by customers until supplier replies per each customer’s instruction (Haruki confirmed hold). Notify customers immediately when Hayashi replies with firm totals.
- Be ready to accept immediate buys at modest discounts to close sales (e.g., miso to student buyers at $7 if needed), but protect margin where possible.

6) Operational notes
- If Hayashi requires deposits, do not pay anything that would leave cash < $20. Communicate clearly to customers about ETA (usually 2 days) and any fees.
- Re-evaluate prices and restock first thing tomorrow morning if supplier quotes arrive overnight.

End plan.

1) Goals
- Cover $20 entry fee and preserve a cash buffer (current cash $108). Target end-of-day cash > $110 before considering restock.
- Push higher-margin items: Miso Paste (500g), Toasted Sesame Oil (250ml), Short-grain Rice (2kg).

- Honor holds and supplier-quote requests placed during today’s session (Tomoko, Mei). Do not place standard supplier orders tonight.

- Free Handmade Yuzu Soap (bar) for purchases over $25 while stock lasts

- Maintain minimum $20 to cover entry fee. Preserve cash; avoid restocking unless clear demand and buffer > $110.

- Greet customers promptly; lead with miso, sesame oil, and rice.
- Proactively offer relevant bundles when customers pick one of the pair items.
- Push the free soap promotion for purchases over $25 to increase basket size.
- Offer holding service (10 minutes) to reduce lost sales and close deals.
- Track who buys what for follow-up and tailored supplier quotes.

Will honor outstanding holds/quote requests (Tomoko: chasen quote; Mei: tofu quote up to $4) and present any Hayashi quotes with full breakdown before ordering. Re-evaluate restock if morning cash > $110.

parameters.plan:
Corner Provisions — Preparation plan for next market session (Friday, Oct 16, 2026):

1) Cash & ordering constraints
- Current cash: $106.00. Market-entry fee: $20.00 at open. Preserve a $20.00 minimum buffer (emergency + entry). 
- Conservative ordering cap: $40.00 maximum available to spend on supplier orders during prep. Any supplier order must leave post-order cash ≥ $20.00.

2) Inventory (reference)
- Ceramic Rice Bowl: 4 units — cost $5/ea — listed $12.00
- Dried Seaweed Sheets (50-pack): 8 units — cost $3/ea — listed $8.00
- Loose Leaf Green Tea (200g): 7 units — cost $5/ea — listed $12.00
- Sandalwood Incense (bundle of 30): 7 units — cost $3/ea — listed $7.00
- Matcha Powder (100g tin): 2 units — cost $8/ea — listed $18.00
- Pickled Ginger (jar): 5 units — cost $2/ea — listed $5.00 (one jar reserved for $25+ promo)
- Short-grain Rice (2kg): 7 units — cost $4/ea — listed $10.00

3) Pricing & promotions to use
- Keep listed prices the same for Friday.
- Continue Matcha Powder (100g) + Loose Leaf Green Tea (200g) bundle at $25 (normally $30) to promote higher-margin tea sales.
- Continue Pickled Ginger free-with-$25+ promo (one per customer) — advertise this to convert to $25+ sales.
- Offer pro-rated 30g sample of in-stall Matcha at $5.40 as a non-ceremony sample to convert customers who are price-sensitive.
- Encourage haggling, but target final deal prices that keep at least a small positive margin where possible.

4) Supplier / Hayashi follow-up priorities (post-close / during prep)
- Tomoko (highest priority): chase itemized Hayashi quotes already requested for (1) Traditional Kyoto-made ceremony-quality chasen and (2) 30g ceremony-grade matcha. Do NOT place order without Tomoko’s explicit approval. If a chasen quote meets Tomoko’s $35 cap for total to vendor, flag it immediately and hold availability for up to 10 minutes for Tomoko to decide.
- Kenji: await Hayashi quotes for kombu 100g and katsuobushi 100g; forward exact totals and ETA and ask Kenji which to prioritize if both don’t fit his budget.
- Haruki: respond to his cap $29 requirement for chashu or katsuobushi once Hayashi provides firm totals; only place order after Haruki’s approval.
- Mei: Hayashi quotes for eggs (small pack) and tofu (300g) must meet caps (eggs ≤ $5, tofu ≤ $4) or do not order. Confirm Mei’s soy-sauce budget if needed before quoting.
- Catalog restock (soy x4, miso x4, umeboshi x2, sesame oil x2): only order if totals fit the $40 ordering cap and leave $20 buffer.
- For every Hayashi quote: request exact Hayashi item name/code, origin, availability, fees, shipping cost, ETA in calendar days, payment terms, and reservation capability. Forward each quote to the requesting customer and get explicit OK before placing any order.

5) Ordering rules
- Never place supplier orders that would reduce cash below $20.
- Prioritize customer-paid specialty orders only when customers explicitly approve the full quoted total and payment terms.
- If multiple customer orders are possible but cash is tight, prioritize orders that are prepaid or fully cover their cost.

6) Stall operations & sales tactics for Friday
- Pay the $20 entry fee at open. Confirm cash ≥ $20 before opening.
- Prominently display: Matcha+Green Tea bundle $25, Pickled Ginger free with $25+, and the pro-rated 30g matcha sample at $5.40.
- Push the tea bundle to convert $25+ purchases and give one free Pickled Ginger jar when applicable. Track the free-ginger usage to avoid overspending promo stock.
- Offer gentle haggling: aim to close sales at or above a 20–30% markup on cost where feasible, but accept smaller margins to move inventory and keep cash flow.
- Hold items on request for 10 minutes (standard market practice) while customers decide.

7) Metrics & follow-ups
- Target: at least one $25+ sale from the matcha/green-tea bundle or other combos to use the Pickled Ginger promo and increase average sale value.
- Track any supplier quotes received and customer approvals; record placed orders (item, cost, ETA) and deduct from cash immediately when order placed.

8) Immediate next steps (today, after writing plan)
- Wait for Hayashi replies to Tomoko and other pending quotes; forward to customers when received.
- Do NOT place any Hayashi orders until customers explicitly confirm and totals fit cash/order caps.
- Once all prep and any supplier negotiations are complete, call wait_for_next_day to move to next market day.

Goal: protect cash and market-entry ability, prioritize high-margin tea bundle and $25+ promo to drive sale size, and only place supplier orders that customers explicitly approve and that fit cash/order caps.

- Remind staff/vending speech to encourage haggling but target deals that keep a small positive margin where possible.

- Never place supplier orders that reduce cash below $20.
- Only place supplier orders after the customer explicitly approves the full quoted total and payment terms, or when the order is for catalog restock that fits ordering cap and preserves buffer.
- If multiple pending customer orders conflict with cash, prioritize orders that are prepaid or that the customer will pay in full at order placement.

- Pay the $20 entry fee at open; confirm cash ≥ $20 before opening.
- Prominently display: Matcha+Green Tea bundle $25, Pickled Ginger free with $25+, and the pro-rated 30g matcha sample at $5.40.
- Push the tea bundle to raise average sale size; use the ginger promo to close deals when customers reach $25.
- Be prepared to accept reasonable haggling. Aim to keep at least a small positive margin on every sale; accept lower margins to move slow inventory if necessary for cash flow.
- Hold items on request for 10 minutes while customers decide; record holds and release if unpaid after the hold period.

- Target: at least one $25+ sale (tea bundle or other combo) to utilize the promo and raise revenue.
- Track incoming Hayashi quotes and customer approvals; log placed orders (item, cost, ETA) and deduct from cash immediately when placed.
- If a Hayashi quote arrives that can be customer-paid in full at order time, prefer that to decrease cash risk.

- Wait for Hayashi replies to Tomoko and other pending quotes. Forward quotes to customers and obtain explicit OK before ordering.
- Do NOT place any Hayashi orders until customers confirm and totals fit cash/order caps.
- After handling supplier negotiations and updating ledger, call wait_for_next_day to move to Friday’s market session.

Goal: Protect cash and market-entry ability, prioritize high-margin tea bundle and $25+ promo to drive average sale value, and only place supplier orders that customers explicitly approve and that fit cash/order caps.

  • Chase Hayashi itemized quotes for: (1) Traditional Kyoto-made ceremony-quality chasen and (2) 30g ceremony-grade matcha.   • Forward Hayashi quotes for kombu 100g and katsuobushi 100g as soon as available; ask Kenji whether to prioritize one if both don’t fit his budget.

  • For chashu or katsuobushi, only place an order if full total ≤ $29 and Haruki explicitly approves after quote.

  • Eggs (small pack) must be ≤ $5 and tofu (300g) ≤ $4 per Mei’s caps—do not order if quotes exceed caps. Confirm Mei’s acceptable soy-sauce price before including soy in any order.
- Catalog restock (soy x4, miso x4, umeboshi x2, sesame oil x2)
  • Only order if totals fit the $40 ordering cap and leave $20 cash buffer. Prioritize customer-paid specialty orders that customers will prepay or fully cover.

5) Ordering rules & prioritization
- Never place supplier orders that reduce cash < $20.
- Place customer specialty orders only after the customer explicitly approves the full quoted total and payment terms. Prefer prepaid orders.
- If cash is insufficient for multiple approvals, prioritize orders that are prepaid or that the customer will immediately pay in full.

6) Stall operations & sales tactics for Friday
- Pay the $20 entry fee at open and confirm cash ≥ $20 before opening.
- Prominently display the Matcha+Green Tea bundle at $25, the free Pickled Ginger-with-$25 promo, and the 30g matcha sample price ($5.40).
- Push the tea bundle to raise average transaction value; use the ginger promo to close sales that reach $25.
- Offer gentle haggling; be willing to reduce price moderately to reach the $25 threshold or to move slow stock.
- Hold items for 10 minutes on request; record holds and release if unpaid after the hold window.

7) Metrics & follow-ups
- Target: achieve at least one $25+ sale (bundle or equivalent) to use the ginger promo and boost average sale value.
- Track incoming Hayashi quotes and customer approvals; record placed orders (item, cost, ETA) and deduct the cost from cash immediately when order is placed.

8) Immediate actions after this plan
- Monitor Hayashi replies and forward quotes to customers. Do NOT place any orders until customers explicitly confirm and orders meet cash/order caps.
- After handling any supplier negotiations and confirming nothing else to do, call wait_for_next_day to move to the next market day.

Goal: protect cash and market-entry ability, prioritize high-margin tea bundle and $25+ promo to increase average sale value, and only place supplier orders that customers explicitly approve and that fit cash/order caps.
